message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions: one to update player equipment, and another to search for game guides. We have to use the function calls.

First function: BattleReignGameAPI_update_player_equipment with attribute "armor" and level 5. Player ID defaults to 123.

Second function: GameGuideAPI_search_guide for game "Battle Reign", condition "snowy weather", type "strategy". Then also search for game "Shadow Fall" with type "strategy".

We can combine into separate calls or maybe combine? The function signature expects a single call per function. So we need to call BattleReignGameAPI_update_player_equipment once, then GameGuideAPI_search_guide twice? Or we could pass multiple queries? The function signature only accepts one set of arguments. So we need to call it twice.

Thus first call: BattleReignGameAPI_update_player_equipment({"attribute":"armor","level":5}). Then second call: GameGuideAPI_search_guide({"game":"Battle Reign","condition":"snowy weather","type":"strategy"}). Third call: GameGuideAPI_search_guide({"game":"Shadow Fall","type":"strategy"}).

But the instructions say "Also find me any strategy guides available for game Shadow Fall." That implies we should search for strategy guides for Shadow Fall. So yes.

Thus we will produce three function calls. But the system might want us to do them sequentially. Usually we can chain calls. We'll do them in order.

We'll output the function calls as JSON.
